checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate. The 'Thick spine' checkpoint was correctly marked as untestable due to the 2D side profile, though the visual implication of thickness is present. All other geometry and material checkpoints align well with the visual evidence. The Router was not too lenient; it correctly identified the limitations of the viewing angle.
artifact_review: The Router identified a texture anomaly in the background (severity 1.5) and slight blur at the junction (severity 1.0). These are valid observations. The background noise is characteristic of AI generation or heavy compression, lacking the micro-detail of a real fabric. The experts did not contradict these findings; the topology auditor found a clean mask, but that does not rule out texture-level artifacts. I agree with the severity ratings; they are minor but noticeable upon close inspection.
alignment_reasoning: The image is a near-perfect match for the 'cleaver' class. The fine-grained classifier gave a very high confidence score (logit 7.59), confirming the specific tool type. The geometry (rectangular blade, short handle) and materials (steel, wood) are visually consistent with the taxonomy. Only one checkpoint was untestable, and all testable ones passed.
artifact_reasoning: The primary artifact is the background texture, which appears noisy and synthetic rather than like a physical cloth. There is also minor softness at the handle-blade junction. While the object structure is sound (confirmed by topology and depth experts), the surface quality of the background prevents a perfect artifact score. It is significantly better than the 'mid' reference (altar) but lacks the crisp, natural detail of the 'high' reference (rifle).
